text:
ryan: FYI pushed release notes draft for 2026-03-21. SBOM scanner flagged a transitive dependency with no license tag in canary-eu. Thinking we should carve out that region and continue. opinions?

marta: paste the scan output pls

ryan: here-- deploy-bot output:
```
deploy-bot: sbom-scan: flagged
component: fastpath-utils@2.1.0 (transitive)
issue: spdx-missing / provenance-unknown
severity: low
affected: canary-eu
```

devon: low severity but provenance-unknown. Policy says notify legal and hold on unknown provenance for 24h.

jules: we can do a regional carveout: 1) pin canary-eu to previous image, 2) set rollout-policy to "limited" for eu until resolved, 3) continue with other regions. That preserves momentum.

sam: agree. operational command?

deploy-bot: redeploy command: `redeploy --cluster=canary-eu --image=registry/redwood/service:20260319@sha256:ef12beef --reason="sbom-carveout-20260321"`

marta: running redeploy now. will also set route weight to 0 for canary-eu traffic if needed.

deploy-bot: redeploy job started (id=2026-4421)

marta: redeploy finished. canary-eu pinned to sha256:ef12beef. health ok. routes set to limited.

ryan: i'll update release notes with short blurb: "EU canary temporarily limited due to SBOM provenance follow-up for transitive component fastpath-utils. No customer impact."

jules: devon can you triage which PR introduced that transitive? add lockfile diff and open quick pin PR.

devon: running dependency diff / git-bisect now. ETA 20m.

legal-qa-bot: recommendation: prefer pin-to-digest + request cosign provenance. If cosign cannot attach for 3rd-party transitive, escalate to security for rollback decision. Document the mitigation in release notes and jira ticket.

sam: i created JIRA INF-2026 with steps and assigned to devon + security.

oncall: thanks for the ping, tagging for visibility. We'll keep monitoring.

devon: bisect result: tokenizer@1.4.3 pulled fastpath-utils. Opening PR to pin tokenizer to 1.4.2 and add SBOM metadata + SPDX tag. PR #854.

ryan: once PR merges can we re-run sbom scan in canary-eu and then lift the carveout?

marta: yes. After PR deploy & cosign, request re-scan. If scan passes, we restore canary-eu and update release notes with follow-up note and changelog entry.

jules: I'll also drop a short runbook snippet under /runbooks/releases/region-carveout.md for future reference.

ryan: release notes updated. small follow-up action: if we don't have provenance within 24h, escalate to security to consider full rollback.

sam: noted and added escalation checklist to JIRA. closing loop for now :white_check_mark:
